how_to_apply: Candidates must apply online through the Commission's website, upsconline.nic.in/ora. The portal has four modules: Account Creation, Universal Registration, and the Common Application Form (CAF), which are common to all UPSC recruitments, plus a fourth, post-specific module for this vacancy.
Create an account and complete the Universal Registration on the portal to receive a Universal Registration Number (URN).
Fill in the Common Application Form (CAF) with personal, educational, and category details, and upload a photograph along with a live photo capture.
Upload a signature signed three times on plain white paper, as per the prescribed format.
Complete the post/vacancy-specific module for Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner within the application window.
Upload supporting documents (proof of date of birth, educational qualification, category certificate, disability certificate, etc.) as applicable.
Pay the application fee online, if applicable, and submit the form before the closing date.
Take a printout of the finally submitted application for future reference.
Applications cannot be withdrawn, and no correction or alteration is allowed after final submission. Candidates are advised to apply well in advance rather than waiting for the closing date.
important_instructions: A candidate must be a citizen of India, or fall under the specific categories of Nepal/Bhutan subjects, Tibetan refugees, or persons of Indian origin migrated from certain countries, as defined in the notification. All correspondence from the Commission will be made through the registered e-mail ID, so candidates must provide a correct and active e-mail address. Persons already in regular Government service must submit a declaration that they have informed their Head of Office/Department of their application. Mobile phones and other electronic/communication devices are strictly banned inside the examination/interview venue. Candidates will undergo mandatory face authentication at the examination venue/interview hall. Furnishing false particulars or suppressing material information can lead to rejection of candidature and debarment from future examinations or Government employment. Candidates are strongly advised to use their Aadhaar Card as the ID document for verification.

content_sections.heading: UPSC APFC Vacancy 2026 Details
content_sections.text: A total of 80 vacancies are notified for the post of Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner. The category-wise break-up is given below. Of the 80 posts, three vacancies are reserved for candidates with benchmark disability (PwBD), covering categories such as blindness and low vision, deaf and hard of hearing, and specified locomotor disabilities, as detailed in the official notification.

rows.category: Of which, reserved for Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD)

content_sections.heading: UPSC APFC Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Essential Qualification: A degree of a recognised university or equivalent. Desirable Qualification: A diploma in Company Law, Labour Laws, or Public Administration. The Commission may relax these qualifications at its discretion for otherwise well-qualified candidates, and the notification specifies criteria the Commission may use for shortlisting if the number of applications is large, including preference for desirable qualifications or relevant experience. Additional age relaxation is available for Ex-Servicemen and Commissioned Officers, Central/UT Government employees, and EPFO employees (up to 5 years), as per the concessions listed in the official notification.

content_sections.heading: UPSC APFC Salary
content_sections.text: The post of Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner carries Level-10 in the Pay Matrix as per the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) . The post is permanent and classified as Central Board Group "A", Non-Ministerial, equivalent to Group-A of the Central Government at the corresponding pay level. The probation period is one year, and the post carries All India Service liability, meaning selected officers may be required to serve anywhere in India.

content_sections.heading: UPSC APFC Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection to the post of Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner is made through a Recruitment Test (RT) followed by a Personality Test/Interview. The syllabus for the Recruitment Test broadly covers General English, Indian Culture and Heritage, developmental issues and the Indian economy, governance and the Constitution of India, general science and computer applications, elementary mathematics, statistics and mental ability, industrial relations and labour codes, principles of accountancy, auditing and insurance, and current events of national and international importance. The Recruitment Test will be held at 84 designated centres across India, including cities such as Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Lucknow, with the full list published in the official notification. Centre allotment follows a first-apply-first-allot basis, subject to a ceiling on candidates per centre (except Chennai, Dispur, Kolkata, and Nagpur).
